title: About
text:
I am a Research Fellow in Statistics at the Department of Economics, Management and Statistics, University of Milano-Bicocca.
I received my PhD in Statistics from the University of Milano-Bicocca in February 2025. My doctoral thesis, Advances in Bayesian Methods: Nonparametric Network Modeling and Scalable Computations, focused on Bayesian nonparametric methods for network data and scalable Bayesian computation.
My research interests include Bayesian statistics, Bayesian nonparametrics, statistical network analysis, computational statistics, and Bayesian modeling of complex data.

title: Research
text:
Current research

Bayesian modeling of network data
My research focuses on Bayesian nonparametric methods for modeling heterogeneous populations of networks. The goal is to develop flexible models that can capture both common structural features and heterogeneity across networks.
In this context, I develop Bayesian models based on nonparametric mixture constructions, together with computational methods for posterior inference and applications to real network data.


Longitudinal brain network analysis
I am also working on Bayesian methods for the analysis of longitudinal brain networks, with applications to neurodegenerative diseases.
The research aims to model changes in brain network topology over time while accounting for heterogeneity across individuals and avoiding the need to fix the number of network communities in advance.

title: Research
text:
Publications

Bayesian Nonparametric Modeling of Heterogeneous Populations of Networks
Francesco Barile, Luis E. Lunagómez, Bernardo Nipoti
Bayesian Analysis, 2026.
This work develops a Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling heterogeneous populations of networks. The model provides a flexible representation of network populations while allowing for the identification of representative network structures and patterns of heterogeneity.
DOI


Control Variate-based Stochastic Sampling from the Probability Simplex
Francesco Barile, coauthor
Statistics and Computing.
This work develops a variance-reduced stochastic sampling method for probability-simplex distributions, with applications to Bayesian models such as latent Dirichlet allocation and mixed-membership stochastic block models.
